messages:
maria nguyen: Quick sync — need to pick a pattern for private control plane traffic from customer VPCs. Two options on the table: 1) PrivateLink/interface endpoints to a proxy fleet in our infra (recommended for least routing complexity) or 2) keep peering + NAT/EIP model where customers route to an EIP/NAT we own. Thoughts on tradeoffs?

alex park: My 2c: PrivateLink avoids cross-account route table bloat and asymmetric routing. Also simpler from a security posture — we get SGs on the ENIs. Downside: per-customer ENI quotas and cost on our side.

samir patel: Peering+EIP feels simpler for small customers but it scales poorly. Every peering is one more acceptance step and peering doesn't work across regions. Also we end up managing a lot of NATs and EIPs (cost + brittle).

jevon: Another angle: If we do PrivateLink we can terminate TLS at our proxy and do auth there, but customers may demand end-to-end TLS to their control plane agents -> that pushes cert management to them or requires mutual TLS.

maria nguyen: Good point. For compliance customers we already support mutual TLS for ingestion endpoints. We could offer two modes: PrivateLink with optional mTLS passthrough, or peering for customers who want direct L3 connectivity.

alex park: Implementation concern: PrivateLink -> each customer gets an interface endpoint in their VPC. That creates ENI count pressure in the AZs where our service is. We could amortize by offering a regional NLB+shared endpoint but that requires cross-account permissioning and more complex AWS PrivateLink product setup.

samir patel: Cost model note: PrivateLink has per-GB data charges and endpoint-hour charges. NAT/EIP model pushes cost into EIPs & NAT hours. We should run a toy model for our 50–500k token/day customers to compare. I can sketch numbers.

infra-bot: Reminder: customer-vpc-eip-allocations.csv updated at 1769002000. (automated)

jevon: Operationally, peering + NAT means we're responsible for routing peering maintenance and BGP is not an option. Troubleshooting customer routes is noisy. PrivateLink centralizes the surface we own which reduces blast radius.

maria nguyen: Long-term refactor idea: offer a 'private connector' product based on PrivateLink today, and evolve to a Transit Gateway + shared services model if customers need hub-and-spoke or large-scale connectivity. Transit GW is heavier but better for multi-account scale.

alex park: Agree on staged approach. Short-term: PrivateLink for new customers, keep peering as legacy path. Medium-term: build a connector service that supports both PrivateLink and TGW attachments so we can migrate customers gradually.

samir patel: We should define the security boundary clearly: where does the control plane trust begin? If the proxy terminates auth, we need to ensure keys never leave the customer VPC for sensitive flows. Maybe we only proxy metadata/auth and establish direct encrypted channels for control messages after handshake.

maria nguyen: Proposal for action items: 1) Samir to produce cost/throughput comparison (PrivateLink vs NAT+EIP) by EOD next week. 2) Alex to draft a PrivateLink deployment pattern doc with ENI quota mitigation strategies. 3) Jevon to enumerate compliance implications (mTLS, audit logs, flow logs) and required changes to the private control plane SLA.

alex park: I'll include a short snippet for endpoint config we can test: ```# example NLB target for PrivateLink
aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name rw-pp-nlb --type network --subnets subnet-a subnet-b
# then create a VPC endpoint service and allow principals
```

maria nguyen: Okay. If no objections, I'll file a lightweight RFC capturing option matrix and the staged migration path. Aim to pick default=PrivateLink for new customers unless they explicitly require peering/TGW. :white_check_mark:

jevon: +1 from infra/security side. Let's also add metrics we will track: per-customer latency delta, ENI count per-az, data transfer cost, and MTTR for networking incidents.

samir patel: I'll start the cost model and add a sample spreadsheet link once ready.

maria nguyen: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC draft in #architecture when ready and tag you.
